speaker: Doctor
text: Since your X-ray shows no fracture or dislocation, let's narrow down the soft tissue injury. Did you have any instability or a feeling that your knee "gave way" when it happened? Additionally, is the pain concentrated on the inner side of the knee, the outer side, or the front?

speaker: Patient
text: 23-year-old female. The patient presents with knee pain that started yesterday and has been steadily worsening. She cites recent participation in volleyball involving repetitive pivoting and twisting movements as a possible cause. She was advised at her last physical exam that weight loss could be beneficial for her health.

speaker: Doctor
text: Based on your history of volleyball with pivoting and twisting, and the worsening pain starting yesterday, is the pain localized to the inside of your knee? Also, does the pain feel worse when you are standing up from a sitting position or climbing stairs?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Knee pain, specifically over the medial aspect of the tibia just inferior to the patella. I also have Recent weight loss attempt, Increased physical activity.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Medial Tibial Stress Syndrome (Shin Splints)

The pain location you described—medial aspect of the tibia just inferior to the patella—is highly characteristic of this condition, especially given your recent increase in physical activity and volleyball participation. Do you feel a dull ache along the inner shin that worsens with walking or running?
